speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning symptoms that require a thorough evaluation. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any recent changes in your bowel habits or the appearance of your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of drenching night sweats, significant weight loss, and fatigue combined with an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node are highly concerning for malignancy or chronic infection. Given the abdominal pain, have you noticed any loss of appetite or early satiety, feeling full very quickly after starting a meal?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of the lymph node as "fixed" and non-tender, combined with your "drenching" night sweats and significant weight loss, raises a high suspicion for lymphoma or metastatic disease. I need to assess how advanced this might be; have you noticed any pain in your abdomen, chest, or back, especially during or after eating? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, LDH, ESR.
